newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED MIXED ON MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES QUOTED MIXED ON MONDAY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted mixed in fairly quiet Monday trade.
Dealers said the Reserve Bank offered Z$500 million worth of treasury bills to discount houses but rejected their bid rates as too high.
"It looks like they are trying to put a cap on the rates," one dealer said.
Meanwhile the discount houses were selling the central bank paper in the secondary market at 16.75 percent from Friday's 16.50 percent.
Call money was at 16 percent from a 17 to 17.25 percentage range while bank bills were at 17.25 percent from 17.75 percent (buying) and eased to 16.50 percent (selling) from 17.25 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold unchanged at 18 percent and 17.50 percent in a market which opened with a surplus of Z$58 million.
